title: Attention Is All You Need: Transformer Architecture for Neural Machine Translation
abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.
citation: Vaswani, A., Shazeer, N., et al. (2017). Attention is all you need. Advances in neural information processing systems, 30.

content.title: Introduction
content.content: Recurrent neural networks, long short-term memory and gated recurrent neural networks in particular, have been firmly established as state of the art approaches in sequence modeling and transduction problems...

content.content: Most competitive neural sequence transduction models have an encoder-decoder structure. Here, the encoder maps an input sequence of symbol representations to a sequence of continuous representations...

subsections.title: Encoder and Decoder Stacks
subsections.content: The encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers. Each layer has two sub-layers...

subsections.title: Attention
subsections.content: An attention function can be described as mapping a query and a set of key-value pairs to an output...

content.title: Experiments
content.content: We conducted experiments on two machine translation tasks: WMT 2014 English-to-German and WMT 2014 English-to-French...

content.title: Conclusion
content.content: In this work, we presented the Transformer, the first sequence transduction model based entirely on attention...

aiSummary: This groundbreaking paper introduces the Transformer architecture, revolutionizing neural machine translation by relying solely on attention mechanisms. Community feedback highlights its efficiency, scalability, and wide applicability beyond NMT. Some discussions focus on computational requirements and potential improvements to the attention mechanism.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
abstract: We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. Unlike recent language representation models, BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers.
citation: Devlin, J., Chang, M. W., Lee, K., & Toutanova, K. (2018). Bert: Pre-training of deep bidirectional transformers for language understanding. arXiv preprint arXiv:1810.04805.

content.title: Introduction
content.content: Language model pre-training has been shown to be effective for improving many natural language processing tasks...

subsections.title: Fine-tuning BERT
subsections.content: Fine-tuning is straightforward since the self-attention mechanism in the Transformer allows BERT to model many downstream tasks...

content.title: Experiments
content.content: In this section, we present BERT fine-tuning results on eleven NLP tasks...

content.title: Conclusion
content.content: Recent empirical improvements due to transfer learning with language models have demonstrated that rich, unsupervised pre-training is an integral part of many language understanding systems...

aiSummary: BERT revolutionizes NLP by introducing bidirectional pre-training using transformers. The community praises its versatility across tasks and strong performance. Discussions center on fine-tuning strategies, computational costs, and comparisons with subsequent models like GPT and RoBERTa.

title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: We trained a large, deep convolutional neural network to classify the 1.2 million high-resolution images in the ImageNet LSVRC-2010 contest into the 1000 different classes. On the test data, we achieved top-1 and top-5 error rates of 37.5% and 17.0% which is considerably better than the previous state-of-the-art.
citation: Krizhevsky, A., Sutskever, I., & Hinton, G. E. (2012). Imagenet classification with deep convolutional neural networks. Advances in neural information processing systems, 25.

content.title: Introduction

aiSummary: AlexNet marked a watershed moment in deep learning, demonstrating the power of CNNs for image classification. Community discussions focus on its historical impact, architectural innovations like ReLU and dropout, and its influence on subsequent computer vision research.
